transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
NATO is holding an emergency session today called by Poland, which wants support after
three Russian cruise missiles were fired into Eastern Polish territory on Friday.
Reporter Terry Schultz reports from Brussels on what Poland hopes to achieve from this
session.
This is more air defense from NATO, and Poland is expected to present proposals for what
specifically it would like to see, including more surveillance capability, more F-35 stationed
there or nearby, so that they can shoot down incoming objects like missiles and drones.
NATO Secretary General Mark Ruta in Warsaw said all NATO allies stand in full solidarity
with Poland.
The US trade representative says a trade deal with Canada is fairly close, echoing recent
optimism on the Canadian side that an interim trade deal might be struck before the end
of the year.
Dan Carpenschuck reports.
That year-end date is crucial.
President Donald Trump has threatened an additional 50 percent tariff on Canada's auto sector
in January if no deal is reached.
In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, US trade representative Jamison Greer said progress
has been made.
The two sides have been meeting since talks collapsed in August.
Greer also says he wants a constructive economic relationship with Canada.
Canadian officials say they're continuing with negotiations rather than risk waiting
out the final two years of the Trump administration.
And Canada-US trade minister Dominic LeBlanc says if an interim trade agreement could be
reached, that could kick-start formal talks around the review of the North American trade
agreement that includes Mexico.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carpenschuck in Toronto.
For the first time since 2020, Americans are expected to travel a little less for Thanksgiving
this year.
And PR's John Stolmas reports on the latest numbers.
AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel 50 miles or more from home this week, a drop
of about one-tenth of a percent after a three-year trend of record highs.
Just under 80 million people will hop in their cars and hit the highway, 200,000 less than
last year.
AAA blames high gas prices for the decrease, although prices have dropped about 20 cents
a gallon from a week ago and 60 cents from last month.
A little less than six million people will travel by plane, down two-tenths of a percent
from last year.
More Americans will use buses and trains to get away, and a record number of people are
booking cruises during the extended Thanksgiving break.
John Stolmas, NPR News.
Over 1,000 Delta flights were delayed yesterday after an automated system that calculates
an aircraft's weight malfunctioned during a busy time ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
The airline said teams had been using manual workarounds to get flights off the ground,
but says the system is now working.
The flight tracking website FlightAware says 189 flights are delayed so far.
You're listening to NPR.
A new report finds about a third of young adults in the U.S. still live with their parents.
As NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports, they are skewing a bit older.
More than 25 million Americans, aged 18 to 34, live with their parents, according to
a new report by Realtor.com.
The overall share is just under its peak during the pandemic.
Most of them are under 25, but the new report finds the share of older adult children back
at home has grown in the past couple decades, and the trend is spreading outside the most
expensive cities to places like Baltimore, Houston, Atlanta, and Las Vegas.
High home prices and high mortgage rates have priced out many would-be first-time buyers.
They've also led some to move in with parents to help save up for a down payment.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
The Hunger Games movie franchise has a lot to celebrate.
The movie "Sunrise on the Reaping" debuted with an estimated $120 million in North American
theaters over the weekend.
It brought in $225 million globally.
That previous chapter, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," grossed about half as much as
for the first four movies of the season.
Amazon MGM Studios' "I Play Rocky" came in second, with 9.3 million.
The comic drama is about the making of "Rocky," and it scored a rare A-plus cinema score.
It follows Sylvester Stallone's struggle to star as Rocky Balboa in the 1976 film "Rocky."
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: NATO holds emergency session at Poland's request after Russian cruise missiles entered Polish territory
US trade representative Jamison Greer says trade deal with Canada is fairly close
AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel for Thanksgiving, a slight dip from last year
Over 1,000 Delta flights delayed after aircraft weight-calculation system malfunctioned
Realtor.com report finds about a third of young adults still live with their parents
Hunger Games prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping" debuts with $120 million in North American theaters
Amazon MGM's "I Play Rocky" takes second place at the weekend box office with $9.3 million
